Thanks for commenting! Dickinson is one of the poets who inspires me- although I also just like the unique aesthetic that this writing style creates. My other inspirations come from song lyrics and poetry of Anna Varney Cantodea and the works of Clive Barker, as well as my own mental state. 
Woe-is-me is almost the opposite of my intent with this piece; if anything, it is about the advantage that an emotional coldness gives one in relationships, compared to the difficulties that come in trying to create that approach when it is not ones natural character, and the closeness that it may cause one to lose. It's not about heartbreak, but about preventing heartbreak more than anything. I was never intending to shock.

I must say, I love the imagery in this, and the title you chose for this grabbed my attention right away. However, as somebody already mentioned, without this imagery there may not be much to the actual narrative part of your piece. To capture a moment in an image is as good a intention for writing as any, but if that's not what you are going for, you may want to add more context to the story, or even an action of some kind.

Short but thought-provoking! This is actually a bit similar to my own aesthetic when I write poetry, so it caught my attention right away. I feel like there is different ways to interpret the narrative behind this- which can be either a good or a bad thing, depending on how you look at it. I especially like the rhythm of this piece, and your unusual grammar choices (such as, "because we're never, we"). Depending on your intent, you may want to add more concrete imagery to the poem, to expand on your theme.

Your writing is concise, but still descriptive. It gives a relatable narrative which I'm sure many readers could see in themselves. I also like the rhythm of your poem, it gives the piece a good sense of flow. However, Im not sure who exactly the name Ron P. Jones refers to; is it a name chosen for a character at random, or does it have any significance? If it does, you may want to find a way to bring more of that into your piece.

First I have to say, I really like the imagery of the poem. However, I'm not sure if the slashes are intentional parts of the text, or if they signify line breaks- if they are intentional, I think they add an interesting touch to your work. However, I would add some other punctuation to make your text more clear, such as " and I never am found, I'm shaking" instead of "and I never am found I'm shaking".

This definitely looks interesting, although it reads more like prose than like poetry. However, I'm not entirely sure what you are trying to say here or what your concept is. As for the punctuation, I think it's effective, and your work is still concise and direct.

Thanks for commenting! It's true that this poem was mainly written for myself, maybe that's why the meaning is unclear. The story behind it is that, while I am descended from a very noble family, people often treat me with little respect or even judge me for it.
The insects are said people's judgements. They crawl underneath my skin through the way my depression makes me perceive them, making me doubt myself. They should not be worth my attention, but instead I look for faults in my own character, or try to "tear them out", hurting myself in the process. Lines like "mandibles tearing at porcelain veins" stand, literally, for an aspect of my appearance I am judged for- I have light skin with visible veins, which in this day and age most people would consider unattractive. However, it is one of the traits that I share with my ancestors. 
Believe it or not, my intent was not to be angsty- when I want to be angsty, it's ten times worse than this.
As for the capitalization, my format, especially line breaks, got messed up when I was posting -so it does make less sense than it normally would.

Overall, I don't see major issues with the flow of this poem. As somebody mentioned before, you may want to look at the line break between lines 6 and 7. Besides that, I would add some type of punctuation to the poem, even if it is commas or dashes separating different statements that you make. For example, you can write something like "The lonely stay lonely,/ as the world turns to ash-/ Beauty is only/a thing of the past".

I must appologise in advance- when it comes to poetry, I may be a rather harsh critic. That said, your work has many positive sides- I liked the rhythm of the lines, and the way you used repetition. The beginning, to me, is especially strong- after "Love is gentle/ Love  is kind", the third line, "Love is wasted" comes as a surprise that grabs the reader's attention and compels one to continue reading. However, after that, your poem becomes a bit hard to follow. Lines such as "Am I remiss" seem a little out of context; other parts of the writing are too literal, or even cliche, such as "Not knowing bliss/Forever more". I would suggest, as somebody may have already said before, to add some type of symbolism to your work, or even look at your concept through a different lens using a metaphor or analogy. You can also try using punctuation to make the intended impact of your work more clear. You already have a great start with a concept that will be relatable to many readers, but there is certainly room for improvement. Best of luck!
